summary: Iteration 6 backend beta-readiness overhaul verified. 29/29 pytest tests PASS. Covered: (1) Auth returns user role + driver car/plate/rating/approved on user record; (2) /api/cars/nearby returns EMPTY when no driver online, and correctly lists the driver EL12345 after POST /driver/online + /driver/location; (3) POST /api/trips/request creates status='searching' and does NOT auto-progress after 5s (asyncio simulator removed); (4) driver/pending → driver/accept (searching→driver_on_way) → driver/trip/{id}/start (→in_trip) → driver/trip/{id}/arrive (→arrived), driver info populated from user record (Tesla Model Y / EL12345), not fake fleet; (5) POST /api/payments/checkout returns checkout_url + session_id, transaction persisted with payment_status=pending, rejects 400 when trip not arrived; GET /api/payments/status/{session_id} returns pending, 404 on unknown; (6) AI guardrails: off-topic 'skriv python-kode' → refusal 'kan jeg dessverre ikke hjelpe'; on-topic taxi/pris query answered normally; (7) GDPR export returns user+trips+ai_messages+payments arrays; DELETE anonymizes trips to '[slettet]' and marks user_id='deleted_*'; admin cannot delete via GDPR (400); (8) Admin invite NEW schema {car, plate, vehicle_type, note} → token; public GET returns car/plate; accept creates driver user with car/plate/vehicle_type/rating=5.0, approved=false, /driver/pending 403 until admin approves; (9) Regressions PASS: /places, /trips/estimate (real OSRM route + polyline geometry), /trips/active, /trips list, /trips/{id}/rate, /trips/{id}/cancel, /settings, /payment-methods, /push/vapid-public-key, /push/subscribe, /trips/{id}/messages passenger↔driver chat.

minor.issue: Response still includes user.driver_id (from user.get('driver_id')). New user schema uses user record fields (car/plate) instead of driver_id → this field is always undefined/null now; can be removed from the response for cleanliness.

Still references trip.driver_id equality with current.get('driver_id') as a fallback ownership check, but driver_id in trip is now the driver's user id (not a legacy fleet id) and current.driver_id doesn't exist for real drivers. The primary driver_user_id path works; the fallback is dead code but not harmful.

action_items: Optional cleanup: remove obsolete driver_id field from /auth/login response and from _load_trip_or_403 fallback since real drivers no longer have that attribute (fleet id was removed).
server.py is 1561 lines — well past the 700-line threshold. Strongly recommend splitting into modules (auth, trips, driver, admin, invites, payments, gdpr, ai, push, apple) before further growth.
Consider adding a compound index on db.trip_messages (trip_id + created_at) for list_trip_messages performance.
Consider Pydantic Field(max_length=500) on TripMessageRequest.text so validation returns 422 uniformly.
critical_code_review_comments: progress_trip is a no-op (good), but /trips/request still tries to notify all online drivers via push best-effort — verified this path does not crash when there are 0 subscriptions.
Stripe checkout uses amount_nok*100 for øre — correct.

GDPR delete anonymizes trips but keeps them for accounting; trip_messages are only cleared where from_user_id==uid, so counter-party messages remain visible with anonymized from_name being retained. Consider whether Norwegian data retention rules require anonymizing the from_name in those docs as well.
/api/cars/nearby cutoff of 60s is tight — if the frontend heartbeat lapses (e.g., tab hidden), the driver silently disappears from nearby. Acceptable for beta but worth exposing in docs.
